desc: Agent Prompt scip-search Contract and Claude Permission: consuming successful available-index metadata from the runtime `scip-search` service, adding structured scip-search prompt data to base prompt construction, rendering the conditional base prompt section with explicit absolute index paths, supported command loop, snapshot semantics, Go/TypeScript/Python capability-specific wording, prompt omission when no indexes are available, and adding `Bash(scip-search:*)` to `internal/embedded/claude-settings.json`. Out of scope: init-time validation, language allowlist persistence, SCIP index generation, lifecycle indexing call-site wiring, README/operator documentation, generated `.claude/settings.json`, and any wrapper or MCP abstraction for `scip-search`.
done_when: Prompt and settings tests prove that: (a) when no successful indexes are supplied, the rendered agent prompt contains no `scip-search` section; (b) when Go, TypeScript, or Python indexes are supplied, the rendered prompt includes each explicit absolute index path in `--index` examples and does not ask agents to infer index locations; (c) the prompt includes the supported `symbols`, `references`, file-open loop, and implementation guidance only where language capability wording permits it; (d) Python guidance says `scip-search implementations` is not supported for Python and does not render a Python implementations command; (e) TypeScript implementation wording is caveated as upstream-supported but not locally verified; (f) the prompt states indexes are snapshots that will not reflect subsequent agent edits; and (g) `internal/embedded/claude-settings.json` is valid JSON whose `permissions.allow` contains `Bash(scip-search:*)`.
scope: In scope: consuming successful available-index metadata from the runtime `scip-search` service, adding structured scip-search prompt data to base prompt construction, rendering the conditional base prompt section with explicit absolute index paths, supported command loop, snapshot semantics, Go/TypeScript/Python capability-specific wording, prompt omission when no indexes are available, and adding `Bash(scip-search:*)` to `internal/embedded/claude-settings.json`. Out of scope: init-time validation, language allowlist persistence, SCIP index generation, lifecycle indexing call-site wiring, README/operator documentation, generated `.claude/settings.json`, and any wrapper or MCP abstraction for `scip-search`.
